title: Cardinal Physical Damage Coverage Recovery Unit Guideline: Fault, Subrogation and Deductible Reimbursement
content:
## Fault

Fault on a Cardinal Physical Damage Coverage collision claim is determined from the police report, the drivers' statements and the physical evidence. The Cardinal driver's share of fault is recorded as a percentage together with the other party's insurance status. A revised determination is recorded as a new determination, and the latest one governs.

The claim counts as an at-fault accident of the Cardinal driver when the Cardinal driver's share of fault is above 50 percent.

## Subrogation

Subrogation is pursued against the other party only when the Cardinal driver's share of fault is below the policy state's bar, for the other party's share of what was paid plus the deductible. When the other party is at fault, Cardinal pursues subrogation for what it paid plus the insured's deductible.

| Policy state | Subrogation bar: pursued only when the Cardinal driver's share is below |
|---|---|
| OH | 51 percent |
| IN | 51 percent |
| KY | 100 percent |
| VA | 1 percent |
| WV | 50 percent |

Boundary illustrations: under an OH policy a share of 50 percent is below the bar and a share of 51 percent is not; under a VA policy only a share of 0 percent is below the bar; a share of exactly 50 percent is not above 50 percent, so it does not make the claim an at-fault accident, while 51 percent does.

## Deductible reimbursement from a subrogation recovery

A subrogation recovery first reimburses the insured's deductible in the same proportion that the recovery bears to the total loss (the net amount paid on the claim plus the deductible): the reimbursement is the deductible applied, multiplied by the recovery amount, divided by the net amount paid on the claim plus the deductible applied, rounded to the cent. The reimbursement is paid to the insured as its own payment tied to that recovery. Deductible Rewards credit used on the claim is restored to the vehicle's credit in the same proportion instead of being paid in cash.

*Worked example (hypothetical figures):* net amount paid on the claim 4500.00, deductible applied 500.00, subrogation recovery 2500.00. The total loss is 5000.00; the recovery is half of it, so the reimbursement is 500.00 multiplied by 2500.00 divided by 5000.00, which gives 250.00, paid to the insured as its own payment.

## Other recovery provisions

- Salvage proceeds are kept by Cardinal and reimburse no deductible.
- A recovery is recorded once per remittance.
- A voided payment reverses its amount from loss paid.
